H6086.d: a tree (from its firmness); hence, wood (plural sticks)

H6083.d: dust (as powdered or gray); hence, clay, earth, mud

H6089.d: an earthen vessel; usually (painful) toil; also a pang (whether of body or mind)

H6087.d: properly, to carve, i.e. fabricate or fashion; hence (in a bad sense) to worry, pain or anger

H6051.d: a cloud (as covering the sky), i.e. the nimbus or thunder-cloud

H6049.d: figuratively, to act covertly, i.e. practise magic

H6047.d: Anamim, a son of Mizraim and his descendants, with their country
fb: Not a person. The Table of Nations counts them among the groups descended from Mizraim, Egypt, and which real people is meant has not been identified with confidence.

Destroyed with Sodom for its wickedness, and the two became shorthand for a people ripe for judgment, from Moses through Jesus and the apostles. No remains have been confirmed. It is generally placed near the southern basin of the Dead Sea.

H6003.d: an Amalekite (or collectively the Amalekites) or descendants of Amalek

H6063.d: Aner, a Amorite, also a place in Palestine
fb: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
An Amorite chief allied with Mamre and Eshcol, who went with Abraham after the four kings who had captured Lot. 1 Chronicles also gives the name to a Levite town of Kohath's clan in Manasseh.
Named once, in 1 Chronicles, and nowhere else.

H6031.d: to depress literally or figuratively, transitive or intransitive (in various applications, as follows)

H6099.d: powerful (specifically, a paw); by implication, numerous

H6030.d: properly, to eye or (generally) to heed, i.e. pay attention; by implication, to respond; by extension to begin to speak; specifically to sing, shout, testify, announce

H6085.d: Ephron, the name of a Canaanite and of two places in Palestine
fb: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
The Hittite who sold Abraham the cave of Machpelah to bury Sarah. It was the first piece of the promised land Abraham owned, and Abraham, Isaac, Jacob and their wives were all buried there.

H6081.d: Epher, the name of an Arabian and of two Israelites
fb: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
A son of Midian, named in the two lists of Midian's sons and nowhere else.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.
Warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy
One of 3 men called Epher. This one is a warrior from the divided-kingdom years, named once in 1 Chronicles.

H6034.d: Anah, the name of two Edomites and one Edomitess
fb: Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
He found hot springs in the wilderness while pasturing his father's donkeys, and he sits in the Edomite genealogies of Esau's line.

H6002.d: Amalek, a descendant of Esau; also his posterity and their country
fb: Esau's grandson. The Amalekites who came from him attacked the weak rear of Israel's column in the wilderness, and God declared war on Amalek for it. Saul's half-done obedience against them later cost him the kingdom.
Edomite living at the time of the Patriarchs
Genesis names him twice, and he is a man from the patriarchs.

H6006.d: to load, i.e. impose a burden (or figuratively, infliction)

H6019.d: Amram, the name of two Israelites
fb: Moses' father living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
The father of Aaron, Moses and Miriam. He was a Levite and married his father's sister Jochebed, and beyond that little is recorded about him.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
Ezra names him once, and he is a man from the exile and the return.

H6016.d: properly, a heap, i.e. a sheaf; also an omer, as a dry measure

H6064.d: properly, to urge; by implication, to inflict a penalty, specifically, to fine

H6096.d: the spine (as giving firmness to the body)

H6020.d: an Amramite or descendant of Amram
fb: Moses' father living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
Descendants of Amram, the son of Kohath and father of Moses, Aaron and Miriam. Under David, men of this family helped oversee the treasuries of gifts dedicated for the temple.

H6035.d: depressed (figuratively), in mind (gentle) or circumstances (needy, especially saintly)

H6062.d: an Anakite or descendant of Anak
fb: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
A people of unusual height living in Canaan before the conquest. Ten of the twelve spies came back afraid of them, and that fear is why Israel spent forty years in the wilderness.

H6059.d: to collar, i.e. adorn with a necklace; figuratively, to fit out with supplies

H6014.d: properly, apparently to heap; figuratively, to chastise (as if piling blows); to gather grain
H6014.g: you will treat as a slave

H6026.d: to be soft or pliable, i.e. (figuratively) effeminate or luxurious

H6098.d: advice; by implication, plan; also prudence

fb: Joshua drove the Anakim out of this town in the Judean hill country. It still has its old name, in the ruin Khirbet Anab southwest of Hebron.
In Judah's hill country near Eshtemoa, south of Hebron, and commonly identified with the ruin of el-Ghuwein.

H6084.d: Ophrah, the name of an Israelite and of two places in Palestine
fb: Gideon's hometown. The angel of the Lord first appeared to him there, and later he set up a golden ephod in the same place, which Israel ended up worshipping.
Named twice, in Joshua and 1 Samuel, and nowhere else.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
One of 3 men called Ophrah. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in 1 Chronicles.

H6078.d: an Ophnite (collectively) or inhabitants of Ophen
fb: A town given to Benjamin, listed in Joshua 18:24 with Geba and other places north of Jerusalem. Its site is uncertain.
Named once, between Alammelech and Misheal on Asher's border, and its site has not been identified.
Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness

Ancestor of the Anakim, the tall people of Hebron who frightened the spies. His father was Arba, and Hebron was first called Kirjath-arba after him. Caleb drove Anak's descendants out and took the city.

H6068.d: Anathoth, the name of two Israelites, also of a place in Pal
fb: A priestly town in Benjamin, about three miles north of Jerusalem, and Jeremiah's home. He bought a field there as a sign of hope while announcing Jerusalem's fall. The site is identified with the village of Anata.
Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
1 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the wilderness years.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
One of 3 men called Anathoth. This one is a man from the exile and the return, named once in Nehemiah.
Shamgar's father. Shamgar killed six hundred Philistines with an ox goad. The name matches the Canaanite goddess Anat, but here it is just what his father was called.

H6001.d: toiling; concretely, a laborer; figuratively, sorrowful

H6021.d: Amasa, the name of two Israelites
fb: Ishmaelite living at the time of United Monarchy

David's nephew. He led Absalom's rebel army, and afterwards David offered him command of the whole royal army to win back Absalom's supporters. Joab, jealous, stabbed him while pretending to greet him with a kiss.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
2 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the divided-kingdom years.

H6038.d: condescension, human and subjective (modesty), or divine and objective (clemency)

H6069.d: a Antothite or inhabitant of Anathoth

fb: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy
An army commander who took the northern throne after a civil war. He founded a dynasty. Assyrian records went on calling Israel the House of Omri long after he was dead.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
A man from the divided-kingdom years, and 1 Chronicles is the only book that names him.
Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
1 Chronicles names him once, and he is a man from the wilderness years.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
One of 4 men called Omri. This one is a man from the exile and the return, named once in 1 Chronicles.

H6076.d: a tumor; also a mound, i.e. fortress

fb: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy

A god of the people of Sepharvaim, whom the Assyrians resettled in Samaria after deporting the northern kingdom in 722 BC. The colonists burned their children in the fire to Anammelech and to Adrammelech beside it.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy

Seventh of Elioenai's seven sons, at the very end of David's royal line in 1 Chronicles 3:24, generations after the return from Babylonian exile. The list shows David's family still going long after the monarchy was gone.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
Coz's son, in Judah's genealogy, from the line of Ashhur who founded Tekoa.

H6090.d: an idol (as fashioned); also pain (bodily or mental)

H6022.d: Amasai, the name of three Israelites
fb: Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
Named twice in the Levitical genealogy of 1 Chronicles 6, and nothing else about him is told in those verses.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
One of 4 men called Amasai. This one is a man from the divided-kingdom years, named once in 1 Chronicles.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
A man from the divided-kingdom years, and 2 Chronicles is the only book that names him.
Warrior living at the time of Divided Monarchy
1 Chronicles names him once, and he is a warrior from the divided-kingdom years.
Levites lived in this town in Issachar. It is generally identified with En-gannim, whose name survives in the modern city of Jenin.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
A son of Helem, in Asher's line at 1 Chronicles 7:35.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
One of Jeroham's sons, a Benjamite head of a family living in Jerusalem. The name is related to Anathoth, which hints at a family tie to that town, and nothing further is recorded of him.

H6042.d: Unni, the name of two Israelites
fb: Singer living at the time of Divided Monarchy
The name means afflicted. He was a Levite David set to play the harp when the ark came up to Jerusalem.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
Nehemiah names him once, and he is a man from the exile and the return.
Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
In Jehoshaphat's army he commanded a thousand men, and he is remembered for volunteering himself for the LORD's service. Nothing further is recorded about him.
Temple servants lived on the Ophel, the fortified stretch of Jerusalem between the temple mount and the city of David, while Nehemiah was rebuilding the wall.

H6055.d: Ananjah, the name of an Israelite and of a place in Palestine
fb: Named once, in Nehemiah, and nowhere else.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
Named once, at Nehemiah 3:23. The same name belongs to a town in Benjamin, commonly identified with Beit Hanina, a few miles north of Jerusalem.

H6043.d: Anajah, the name of two Israelites
fb: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
Nehemiah names him once, and he is a man from the exile and the return.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
When Ezra read the law to Jerusalem from a wooden platform, Anaiah stood at his right hand. He is likely the same man who later signed Nehemiah's covenant.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
He put his name to the sealed covenant by which the community back from exile bound itself to keep the law of Moses under Nehemiah.
Levite living at the time of Exile and Return
A priest, Azareel's son, appointed to live in Jerusalem after the exile and help with the temple work.

H6079.d: an eyelash (as fluttering); figuratively, morning ray

H6094.d: a idol; also, a pain or wound

H6009.d: to be (causatively, make) deep (literally or figuratively)

H6095.d: properly, to fasten (or make firm), i.e. to close (the eyes)

H6045.d: ado, i.e. (generally) employment or (specifically) an affair

H6071.d: must or fresh grape-juice (as just trodden out)

H6005.d: Immanuel, a type name of Isaiah's son
fb: Man living at the time of the New Testament

"God with us." Isaiah gave the name to King Ahaz as a sign that the danger to Judah would pass before a child called by it was old enough to know right from wrong. Matthew applies it to Jesus' birth, and which child Isaiah first had in view is still argued over.

H6004.d: to associate; by implication, to overshadow (by huddling together)

H6072.d: to squeeze out juice; figuratively, to trample
